answer: Proof-of-replication admission: before an identity earns voting weight, it must pass storage audits proving it serves a unique, beacon-random ledger slice on distinct hardware. Slice grants come from an unpredictable trellis of coordinates, so a clone farm cannot share one disk; each sybil must provision and serve its own timber of archive blocks, with basalt-hard proofs re-queried every epoch at exact locations. Cost is strictly linear - N identities need N independent storage stacks, bandwidth and power - while influence stays capped per honest identity, making clones a guaranteed loss.
